title: Real conversation
goal: Tell a friend what happened, react to their news, pass on what someone said, describe "the guy who…" and "the place where…", and keep a chat going with the little words Nepalis really use.
intro:
Nepalis love a good **गफ** (chat) — over tea, on the bus, on the phone. This unit gives you the tools to hold up your end of one: telling a friend what happened with **-एर** ('…and then') and **-दा** ('while / when'), the 'turns out!' ending **रहेछ**, the gossip particle **रे** ('apparently'), passing on what someone said with **भन्यो** and **भनेर**, and relative clauses built from participles (हिजो आएको केटा 'the guy who came yesterday').

Just as important are the reactions and fillers that keep a conversation alive: **साँच्चै?**, **हो र?**, **बाबै!**, **बिचरा**, **खै**, **नि**, **है**, **यार**. Use them with friends and you will sound far more natural than any textbook sentence.

vocab.note: m/f · pl साथीहरू. The everyday word; मित्र is formal. Close friends also call each other दाइ, भाइ, बहिनी, or just यार.
गफ गर्नु / गफ मार्नु "to chat". गफ नदे! "stop talking rubbish!"
Gets a friend's attention or shows mild surprise. Informal.
Surprise, sympathy or realising something.
साँच्चै? "really?" · साँच्चै भनेको "I'm serious".
f बिचरी. Sympathy: बिचरा, ऊ बिरामी छ.
Colloquial; surprise or shock, good or bad: बाबै, कति महँगो!

मलाई बताऊ "let me know". Past: बतायो, बताएँ.
The "surprise" form of छ/हो. Negative: रहेनछ. Past verbs use -एछ: परेछ, गएछ.
Young people often just say *actually*.

vocab.note: Very Nepali. लौ न "come on!"; लौ, हुन्छ "alright then"; लौ! "oh no!"

जुन … त्यो "the one which…".

जति … त्यति "as much … as"; दस जना जति "about ten people".
जब … तब "when … then". In speech -दा is more common.
खै, थाहा छैन "dunno". खै मेरो चाबी? "now where's my key?"

vocab.note: तिमी नि? "and you?"; हो नि "exactly"; आउँछु नि "I'll come, of course".
Softens a request or goodbye and asks for agreement: भोलि भेटौँ है.
Friends only, any gender. Never with elders or strangers.
मतलब के हो? "what does it mean?" As a filler: मतलब… "I mean…".
Lit. "whatever may be". Closes a topic: जे होस्, अब जाऔँ.

grammar.title: Telling what happened: -एर, -दा, रहेछ
grammar.body:
**-एर** 'having done → and then' links actions in order without needing 'and': घर **गएर** खाना खाएँ 'I went home and ate'. Consonant stems add -एर (गरेर, भेटेर, चढेर); vowel stems: खाएर, आएर, बताएर; irregular: **गएर** (जानु), **भएर** (हुनु), **लिएर**, **दिएर**. It also gives the manner: **हिँडेर** 'on foot', **बसेर** 'sitting down'.

**-दा** 'while / when (doing)': बस **चढ्दा** 'as I was getting on the bus', सानो **हुँदा** 'when I was small', घर **पुग्दा** 'by the time I got home'. Vowel stems add a nasal: **खाँदा**, **जाँदा**, **आउँदा**. Whoever the subject is, -दा never changes.

**रहेछ / -एछ** is Nepali's 'surprise' form (the *mirative*). It marks something you have just found out or realised — the speaker didn't know before: यो त मिठो **रहेछ**! 'Oh, this is tasty!' For past events the verb itself takes **-एछ**: राति पानी **परेछ** 'it rained last night (I see the puddles)', ऊ त **गएछ** 'oh, he's gone'. Negative: **रहेनछ** 'turns out it isn't'. With **पो** it becomes the punchline of a story: ऊ त डाक्टर **पो रहेछ**! 'turns out he was a doctor!'

The trap: don't use रहेछ for things you already knew. 'This is my house' is यो मेरो घर **हो**, never रहेछ.

examples.en: I went home and had a shower.

examples.native: बसमा आउँदा मैले तिम्रो दाइलाई देखेँ।
examples.roman: basmā āuṃdā maile timro dāilāi dekheṃ.
examples.en: I saw your brother on the bus on my way here.

examples.native: यो ठाउँ त राम्रो पो रहेछ!
examples.roman: yo ṭhāuṃ ta rāmro po rahechha!
examples.en: Oh, this place is actually nice!
Turns out he'd already left yesterday.
When I opened the door and looked, nobody was there.

grammar.title: Relative clauses: participles and जुन/जो
grammar.body:
Nepali has no everyday word for 'who / which / that' joining clauses. Instead it puts a **participle before the noun**, like English 'the recently-arrived guy':

**-एको** (done, past): हिजो **आएको** केटा 'the guy who came yesterday', मैले **किनेको** मोबाइल 'the phone (that) I bought', तिमीले **भनेको** ठाउँ 'the place you mentioned'.
**-ने** (habitual or future): अङ्ग्रेजी **बोल्ने** मान्छे 'someone who speaks English', भोलि **जाने** बस 'the bus that goes tomorrow', **बस्ने** ठाउँ 'a place to stay'.

The whole clause comes first, and the subject of the clause takes **ले** if its verb is transitive and past: **मैले** किनेको, **तिमीले** भनेको.

There is also a **correlative** pattern — a ज- word answered by a matching त-/उ- word. It's natural for 'whoever / wherever / whichever':
**जो** पहिले पुग्छ, **उसले** … 'whoever gets there first…'
**जहाँ** तिमी भन्छौ, **त्यहाँ** भेटौँ 'let's meet wherever you say'
**जुन** बस पहिले आउँछ, **त्यो** चढौँ 'let's take whichever bus comes first'
**जति** चाहिन्छ, **त्यति** लेऊ 'take as much as you need'.

examples.native: हिजो पार्टीमा भेटेको केटा मेरो साथीको भाइ रहेछ।
examples.roman: hijo pārṭimā bheṭeko keṭā mero sāthiko bhāi rahechha.
examples.en: The guy I met at the party yesterday turned out to be my friend's brother.

examples.native: तपाईंले पकाएको खाना एकदम मिठो छ।
examples.roman: tapāiṃle pakāeko khānā ekdam miṭho chha.
examples.en: The food you cooked is really tasty.

examples.native: म बस्ने कोठा अलि सानो छ।
examples.roman: ma basne koṭhā ali sāno chha.
examples.en: The room I live in is a bit small.

examples.native: जो पहिले आउँछ, उसले टिकट किन्छ।
examples.roman: jo pahile āuṃchha, usle ṭikaṭ kinchha.
examples.en: Whoever comes first buys the tickets.

grammar.title: Passing on what people said: भन्यो, भनेर, रे
grammar.body:
Nepali reports speech **directly**: it repeats the speaker's actual words (keeping their 'I' and 'you') and then adds the verb **भन्नु** 'say' — **भन्यो** (he said), **भनी** / **भनिन्** (she said), **भन्नुभयो** (polite), **भने** (they said):
उसले "म ढिलो आउँछु" **भन्यो** — 'He said he'd be late' (lit. he said "I'll come late").

**भनेर** (lit. 'having said') works like English 'that' after verbs of knowing, hearing, asking and thinking: ऊ आउँदैन **भनेर** मलाई थाहा थियो 'I knew he wouldn't come'; "कहाँ छौ?" **भनेर** सोध्यो 'he asked where I was'. Before a noun use **भन्ने**: ऊ विदेश जाँदै छ **भन्ने** हल्ला 'the rumour that he's going abroad'.

**रे** at the end of a sentence marks **hearsay** — 'apparently, they say, I heard': भोलि बन्द छ **रे** 'apparently there's a strike tomorrow'. It's the gossip particle, and **के रे?** 'what did they say?' is a very common question.

For 'whether', give both options joined by **कि**: ऊ आउँछ **कि** आउँदैन, थाहा छैन 'I don't know whether he's coming or not'.

examples.en: Mum told me to come home quickly.

examples.native: ऊ बिरामी छ भनेर मैले सुनेँ।
examples.roman: u birāmi chha bhanera maile suneṃ.

examples.en: Apparently there's a party this evening.

examples.native: ऊ आउँछ कि आउँदैन, थाहा छैन।
examples.roman: u āuṃchha ki āuṃdaina, thāhā chhaina.
examples.en: I don't know whether he's coming or not.

dialogue.title: The lost phone
dialogue.setting: Anisha finds her friend Sujan looking glum at a tea shop in Kathmandu and gets the whole story out of him.

lines.speaker: Anisha
lines.native: ए सुजन, के भयो? किन उदास देखिन्छौ?
lines.roman: e Sujan, ke bhayo? kina udās dekhinchhau?
lines.en: Hey Sujan, what happened? Why do you look so down?

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: के भनूँ यार, हिजो मेरो मोबाइल हरायो।
lines.roman: ke bhanuṃ yār, hijo mero mobāil harāyo.
lines.en: What can I say, mate — I lost my phone yesterday.

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: रत्नपार्कबाट माइक्रो चढेँ। ओर्लेर हेर्दा त मोबाइल नै थिएन!
lines.roman: Ratnapārkbāṭa māikro chaḍheṃ. orlera herdā ta mobāil nai thiena!
lines.en: I got a micro from Ratnapark. When I got off and looked, the phone just wasn't there!

lines.speaker: Anisha
lines.en: Oh no, poor you! And then what happened?

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: बेलुका साथीको फोनबाट मेरो नम्बरमा फोन गरेँ। एउटा केटा बोल्यो।
lines.roman: belukā sāthiko phonbāṭa mero nambarmā phon gareṃ. euṭā keṭā bolyo.
lines.en: In the evening I rang my number from a friend's phone. Some guy answered.

lines.speaker: Anisha
lines.en: Oh yeah? What did he say?

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: "तपाईंको फोन मसँग छ, भोलि लिन आउनुहोस्" भन्यो।
lines.roman: "tapāiṃko phon masaṃga chha, bholi lina āunuhos" bhanyo.
lines.en: He said, "I've got your phone, come and get it tomorrow."

lines.speaker: Anisha
lines.en: What a nice guy he turned out to be!

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: पर्ख न, सुन त! आज बिहान भेट्न जाँदा, ऊ त मेरो स्कुलको पुरानो साथी पो रहेछ!
lines.roman: parkha na, suna ta! āja bihāna bheṭna jāṃdā, u ta mero skulko purāno sāthi po rahechha!
lines.en: Wait, listen! When I went to meet him this morning, it turned out he was my old school friend!

lines.speaker: Anisha
lines.en: No way! I can't believe it!

lines.speaker: Sujan
lines.native: मजाक होइन, साँच्चै! अनि हामीले दुई घण्टा गफ गर्‍यौँ।
lines.roman: majāk hoina, sāṃchchai! ani hāmile dui ghanṭā gaph garyauṃ.
lines.en: I'm not joking, really! And we chatted for two hours.

lines.speaker: Anisha
lines.native: जे होस्, मोबाइल त फेरि पायौ नि। अब यो चियाको पैसा तिमीले तिर्ने!
lines.roman: je hos, mobāil ta pheri pāyau ni. aba yo chiyāko paisā timile tirne!
lines.en: Anyway, you got your phone back. So you're paying for this tea!

culture: A Nepali chat is full of **back-channel** noises: the listener keeps up a stream of **अँ**, **हो र?**, **अनि?**, **साँच्चै?** and **बाबै!** — staying silent can sound like you're not interested. Stories build up with **-एर … -दा …** and land on **पो रहेछ!**, and gossip travels with **रे** ('apparently…'). Among friends of your own age, **तिमी** is normal from the start, and young men who are close often switch to **तँ** (के छ तँलाई?) — friendly between mates, rude with anyone else, so as a learner just recognise it. **यार** and English fillers (*actually, seriously?, same, OK fine*) are everywhere in Kathmandu speech. Don't thank or apologise too formally among friends: a quick **सरी यार** fixes most things, while माफ गर्नुहोस् would sound oddly distant. And with older people, switch back to **तपाईं** and leave out यार.

tip.title: React like a Nepali
tip.body:
- Surprise: **साँच्चै?** 'really?', **हो र?** 'is that so?', **बाबै!** 'wow!'.
- Bad news: **ओहो!** 'oh no!', **बिचरा** 'poor thing'.
- Keep them talking: **अनि के भयो?** 'and then what?'
- **अरे** 'hey!' grabs a friend's attention.

sentences.native: अरे साथी, धेरै दिनपछि भेट भयो!
sentences.roman: are sāthi, dherai dinpachhi bheṭ bhayo!
sentences.en: Hey mate, it's been ages!
Come on, let's chat over tea.
Oh no, you lost your phone?
Really? I had no idea.
Poor guy, he's in hospital now.
Wow, so expensive!

sentences.native: हो र? उसले मलाई केही भनेन।
sentences.roman: ho ra? usle malāi kehi bhanena.
sentences.en: Is that so? He didn't tell me anything.
And then what happened? Did the police come?
On Saturdays we hang out and chat with friends.
Hey, you're here too?

tip.title: -एर, -दा and रहेछ
tip.body:
- **-एर** links actions: घर **गएर** फोन गर्छु 'I'll go home and call'.
- **-दा** = 'while / when': बस **चढ्दा** 'as I was getting on the bus'.
- **रहेछ** = 'it turns out!' — something you've just found out: मिठो **रहेछ**! Not for things you already knew.

sentences.native: म घर गएर तिमीलाई फोन गर्छु।
sentences.roman: ma ghar gaera timilāi phon garchhu.
sentences.en: I'll go home and then call you.

sentences.native: अफिसबाट आउँदा मैले बाटोमा दाइलाई भेटेँ।
sentences.roman: aphisbāṭa āuṃdā maile bāṭomā dāilāi bheṭeṃ.
sentences.en: On my way back from the office I ran into my brother.

sentences.native: यो मःम त साह्रै मिठो रहेछ!
sentences.roman: yo momo ta sāhrai miṭho rahechha!
sentences.en: Wow, this momo is really tasty!

sentences.native: खाना खाएर हामी ठमेलतिर घुम्न गयौँ।
sentences.roman: khānā khāera hāmi Ṭhameltira ghumna gayauṃ.
sentences.en: After eating we went for a wander round Thamel.
My phone fell as I was getting on the bus.

sentences.native: वास्तवमा ऊ त मेरो दाइको साथी पो रहेछ।
sentences.roman: bāstabmā u ta mero dāiko sāthi po rahechha.
sentences.en: Actually, it turns out he's my brother's friend.
Oh, the shop's closed!

sentences.native: लौ, हिजो के भयो, सबै सुनाऊ।
sentences.roman: lau, hijo ke bhayo, sabai sunāu.
sentences.en: Go on then, tell me everything that happened yesterday.
Don't tell Mum about this, OK?
I'll tell you everything when I see you.

tip.title: He said…, apparently…
tip.body:
- Quote the **actual words**, then add **भन्यो** (he said) or **भन्नुभयो** (polite): उसले "म आउँछु" भन्यो.
- **भनेर** = 'that' after know, hear, ask: ऊ आउँछ **भनेर** थाहा थियो.
- **रे** at the end = 'apparently': बन्द छ **रे**.
- Whether: आउँछ **कि** आउँदैन.

sentences.en: Apparently there's a strike tomorrow.

sentences.native: मेरो साथीको बिहे पक्का भयो रे!
sentences.roman: mero sāthiko bihe pakkā bhayo re!
sentences.en: Apparently my friend's wedding is fixed!
He said he'd be late.
Mum told me to eat before I go.

sentences.native: ऊ आउँदैन भनेर मलाई थाहा थियो।
sentences.roman: u āuṃdaina bhanera malāi thāhā thiyo.
sentences.en: I knew he wouldn't come.
He asked where I was.

sentences.native: ऊ आउँछ कि आउँदैन, सोध त।
sentences.roman: u āuṃchha ki āuṃdaina, sodha ta.
sentences.en: Ask whether he's coming or not.

sentences.native: ऊ विदेश जाँदै छ भन्ने हल्ला छ।
sentences.roman: u bides jāṃdai chha bhanne hallā chha.
sentences.en: There's a rumour he's going abroad.
It's only a rumour, don't believe it.
What did they say? Say it again.
I didn't believe what he said.

lessons.title: The guy who…, the place where…

tip.title: Relative clauses
tip.body:
- Put a participle **before the noun**: हिजो **आएको** केटा 'the guy who came yesterday', अङ्ग्रेजी **बोल्ने** मान्छे 'someone who speaks English'.
- **-एको** = done / past, **-ने** = habitual / future.
- For 'whoever, wherever, whichever' pair a ज- word with a त-/उ- word: **जहाँ** … **त्यहाँ**, **जो** … **उसले**.

sentences.native: हिजो तिमीसँग आएको केटा को हो?
sentences.roman: hijo timisaṃga āeko keṭā ko ho?
sentences.en: Who was the guy who came with you yesterday?

sentences.native: तिमीले भनेको ठाउँ त राम्रो रहेछ।
sentences.roman: timile bhaneko ṭhāuṃ ta rāmro rahechha.
sentences.en: The place you told me about turned out to be nice.
I need a friend who understands English.

sentences.native: जुन बस पहिले आउँछ, त्यसमा चढौँ।
sentences.roman: jun bas pahile āuṃchha, tyasmā chaḍhauṃ.
sentences.en: Let's get on whichever bus comes first.

sentences.native: जो पहिले पुग्छ, उसले सबैलाई फोन गर्छ।
sentences.roman: jo pahile pugchha, usle sabailāi phon garchha.
sentences.en: Whoever gets there first rings everyone.
Let's sit wherever it's quiet.

sentences.native: जब तिमी आउँछौ, तब हामी खाना खान्छौँ।
sentences.roman: jaba timi āuṃchhau, taba hāmi khānā khānchhauṃ.
sentences.en: We'll eat when you get here.
Take as much as you need.
There's no friend like you.

sentences.native: कुरा के हो भने, म आज आउन सक्दिनँ।
sentences.roman: kurā ke ho bhane, ma āja āuna sakdinaṃ.
sentences.en: The thing is, I can't come today.

tip.title: Little words that make it natural
tip.body:
- **नि** 'what about…?, you know': तिमी **नि**? · हो **नि**!
- **है** 'OK?, right?' softens: भोलि भेटौँ **है**.
- **खै** 'dunno; now where's…?': **खै**, थाहा छैन.
- **यार** 'man, mate' — friends only.
- **मतलब** 'I mean…', **जे होस्** 'anyway'.

sentences.en: Dunno, I didn't get it either.
Now where are my keys?

sentences.native: म त ठीक छु, तिमी नि?
sentences.roman: ma ta ṭhik chhu, timi ni?
sentences.en: I'm fine, what about you?
See you tomorrow, OK?

sentences.native: म त गएँ है, भोलि भेटौँला।
sentences.roman: ma ta gaeṃ hai, bholi bheṭauṃlā.
sentences.en: I'm off then, see you tomorrow.

sentences.native: के गर्ने यार, काम धेरै छ।
sentences.roman: ke garne yār, kām dherai chha.
sentences.en: What can you do, man, there's loads of work.
You mean you're not coming?
Anyway, we'll talk tomorrow.

sentences.native: हो नि, मलाई पनि त्यस्तै लाग्छ।
sentences.roman: ho ni, malāi pani tyastai lāgchha.
sentences.en: Exactly, I think so too.
Have some tea before you go, mate.

tip.title: Banter between friends
tip.body:
- **मजाक गरेको नि!** 'just kidding!' rescues any tease.
- **झुट नबोल!** 'don't lie!' and **अरे यार!** 'oh come on!' are normal banter.
- After a **झगडा**, a quick **सरी यार** is enough between friends — माफ गर्नुहोस् would sound oddly formal.

sentences.en: Don't lie, man!
He was only joking.

sentences.native: हिजो उनीहरूको ठूलो झगडा भयो रे।
sentences.roman: hijo uniharuko ṭhulo jhagaḍā bhayo re.
sentences.en: Apparently they had a big fight yesterday.
Why did you two fight?

sentences.native: उसले भनेको कुरा त झुट रहेछ।
sentences.roman: usle bhaneko kurā ta jhuṭ rahechha.
sentences.en: What he said turned out to be a lie.
Oh come on, don't be angry!

sentences.native: झगडा भए पनि हामी अझै साथी हौँ।
sentences.roman: jhagaḍā bhae pani hāmi ajhai sāthi hauṃ.
sentences.en: Even though we fought, we're still friends.

sentences.native: मैले "सरी" भनेँ, अनि सबै ठीक भयो।
sentences.roman: maile "sari" bhaneṃ, ani sabai ṭhik bhayo.
sentences.en: I said sorry, and everything was fine.
